content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: chat deflection, delayed breaks, general callback and a cancelled late payments coaching session lift service level to 80.4% (target 80%) for ₹3,687.","why":"Unplanned absence (bus-strike lateness plus sickness) has left both queues about 6–7 agents short while call volume is on plan. With no action, service level for 09:45–15:30 is predicted at 68.3%, with 6.8% abandons. P2 reduces demand by moving 20% of simple status and balance enquiries to chat, delays the 09:45–10:30 breaks by 45 minutes, adds callback on general and cancels the 15:30–16:00 payments coaching. The result is a predicted 80.4% service level (payments 78.5%, general 82.9%), abandons falling to 4.4%, and 85.7% for the rest of the day. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target and it breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["P4 adds overtime on both queues for 82.9% (payments 81.8%) and 3.7% abandons, but costs ₹6,567, ₹2,880 more than P2, for a modest gain.","P3's payments-only overtime costs ₹2,880 but reaches only 69.8%, so extra staff alone does not close the gap at that scale.","P1 (no cost) does worse than no action, 65.9% vs 68.3%, so the breaks and callback only work when combined with deflection.","Payments stays slightly under target at 78.5% under P2, while general carries the overall figure at 82.9%."],"watch":"Watch payments service level first, as it is the queue below 80%. Check that chat is absorbing the deflected enquiries without a backlog building. If the strike-delayed staff arrive, capacity will improve and you may be able to restore breaks or the coaching session. If payments keeps slipping, P4's payments overtime is the next step."}
